findings.claim: Step 1 sets the typesafe provider's base_url to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone, but the 2.3.1 provider appends /v1/systemone (decisions) and /v1/models (listing) to base_url itself, so every Jev call goes to .../v1/systemone/v1/systemone. A non-default base_url also turns off the pinned jev catalog and reports a failed listing instead of falling back to it, so a typesafe/ model can also be missing from the catalog. The outcome's typesafe/ decision call returning 200 cannot pass as written. Fix: leave base_url out (default https://api.typesafe.ai) or set it to the bare host.

No spike measured clef:cloud on ollama.com. All four router spikes used a mock upstream. The decision classifier's default timeout is 1500 ms; on a timeout or upstream error Bifrost publishes no complexity tier, none of the three tier rules match, and router-key chats go to the requested model with only a warning log. The router would then look deployed but never route, and the outcome's simple-to-gpt-oss / hard-to-mistral-large-4 check fails. The timeout is settable (governance.complexity_analyzer_config.decision.timeout), so the plan needs a measured value or evidence that the default holds. Spike question: with an Ollama Cloud key, how long do several POST https://ollama.com/v1/systemone calls to clef:cloud with a three-choice complexity question take (p50/max), and do gpt-oss:120b-cloud, deepseek-v4.1-flash and mistral-large-4 answer a chat call on ollama.com under those exact names? gpt-oss:120b-cloud and mistral-large-4 appear nowhere else in the repo.
Step 1 now adds the typesafe provider with no base_url, so the provider's own /v1/systemone and /v1/models paths and its built-in Jev model list apply.

Spike 7 measured ollama/clef:27b through the live gateway (5 of 5 at 200, worst 840 ms) and confirmed the three tier models answer under the exact names; the build sets the classifier timeout to 3000 ms.

The smoke check 'hermes not rerouted' cannot show that a Hermes chat makes no classifier call, though the plan's outcome, ADR 0029 and the component page all claim it. The tier rules are router-only, so a Hermes chat keeps its model even if the classifier runs for it (spike 2's exact failure mode). Bifrost reports the classifier call in extra_fields.routing_metadata.calls as a request_type 'decisions' entry (spike 1 stdout). The Hermes check should assert no such entry, and the router check should assert one is present, with a stub test for each.

test_router_key's cloud-suffix scan covers only the classifier, the routing-rule targets and the router key. Row r3 covers every model name in the jobspec and every virtual key in services.tf. It skips the hermes, memex and openviking keys' allowed_models and the provider keys' models lists, so adding 'gpt-oss:120b-cloud' to the Hermes key would pass. Today they are all '*', so the row holds, but the test would not catch a regression there.

entries.change: chat checks read extra_fields.routing_metadata.calls; router chats must make a decisions call, a Hermes chat must make none
stub gateway returns classifier calls with each cases for missing and unexpected calls; the cloud-suffix check in test_router_key now scans every provider key and every virtual key's allowed_models
the claim that the key refuses an unlisted rule target is marked as not measured

findings.claim: the Hermes smoke check passed even when the classifier ran for Hermes
the r3 cloud-suffix scan was narrower than the row
